Backend: 26/26 pytest cases pass (auth email/phone, cookie auth, 401 on protected endpoints, seeded content/org/penalty, cron secret enforcement, full timesheet approval flow, weekly review chain-of-command escalation to admin, feedback forward+resolve, admin content/AI-enhance/penalty/broadcast/employee CRUD incl. deactivate-blocks-login). critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 736 lines — approaching the 700-line threshold; consider splitting into routers (auth, timesheets, reviews, feedback, admin, cron).
CORS_ORIGINS in backend/.env is set to '*' but middleware uses FRONTEND_URL explicitly — CORS_ORIGINS is dead config; either wire it or drop it.
seed() uses @app.on_event('startup') which is deprecated in modern FastAPI; switch to lifespan handlers.
verify_password uses bcrypt.checkpw directly — good — hashes verified to start with $2b$. Bcrypt hashing follows playbook.
Cookie secure=True + samesite='none' is correct for cross-site preview URL; only works over HTTPS (which the preview is).
No brute-force lockout on /api/auth/login — the auth playbook usually recommends 5-fail lockout; not implemented here (minor, not in scope).
AI enhance endpoint takes 5-30s — no explicit request timeout on backend; consider adding an asyncio timeout wrapper to avoid worker hang.

Review-chain ObjectId bug was fixed; prior DB reviews created before the fix may still have ObjectId in chain — serialize() now recursively converts them.
rca of the issue: GET /api/reviews/pending returned 500 with `TypeError: 'ObjectId' object is not iterable`. Reproduction: submit a review, have first approver approve it (which appends {approver_id: ObjectId(...), ...} to chain and moves current_approver_id up), then next approver GETs /reviews/pending. FastAPI attempts to serialize the ObjectId inside chain[].approver_id and fails. Fix: (a) store approver_id as string in chain/history entries during approve/reject/forward, (b) make serialize() also walk chain/history lists and stringify any ObjectId values found inside.
